content:
I got this message on PR #41498

Could you investigate how hard it would be for field_simp to support Ring.inverse?

The idea would be that statements such as this:

have h1 : ((1 - r)⁻¹ʳ) ^ 2 = (1 - r) * ((1 - r)⁻¹ʳ) ^ 3 := by
    rw [pow_succ' _ 2, ← mul_assoc,
      Ring.mul_inverse_cancel _ (isUnit_one_sub_of_norm_lt_one h), one_mul]

could be closed using field_simp; ring.

I have limited experience with metaprogramming so what I've found is that it seems pretty hard to do this. Looking at FieldSimp.lean it seems the algorithm needs a CommGroupWithZero instance (which we don't have in the example above), so it can use commutativity to simplify the goal and also requires statements of the form x ≠ 0 to cancel terms, whereas with Ring.inverse we would need IsUnit x.

Is this something worth building as a separate tactic? Or maybe I have misjudged the complexity of the problem and it's actually easy to do?
CC @Arend Mellendijk @Heather Macbeth

Indeed, field_simp assumes commutativity throughout its current algorithm. Generalising field_simp to mostly just assume CommGroup is doable (and would be a great student project; it would also give a multiplicative version of the abel tactic through field_simp's machinery). Lifting commutativity is much harder.
I would say supporting Ring.inverse is out of scope --- but am interested in hearing what Arend or Heather think.
